clue.text: Its absence would be apparent if it is

definitions.text: Its absence would be apparent if it is

parts.words: Its absence would be apparent if it is
parts.note: the clue's own phrase 'it is' contracts to 'it's'; drop the mark and you get the possessive 'its', so the missing punctuation shows

explanation.surface: A riddle about something whose absence would be obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue points at its own words: 'it is' shortens to IT'S, and without the little raised comma that becomes ITS, which is how the clue begins.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark shows where letters have been dropped in a contraction such as it's.

clue.text: Company faces awesome fine, keeping dry bits of paper

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the shuffled word wraps around the next piece
something awesome knocks you sideways, so the word fine is thrown into a new order

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means dry in the sense of not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A firm is hit with an enormous penalty while staying alcohol-free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company faces' puts CO in front. 'awesome' rearranges FINE to NFEI, and 'keeping' puts TT inside it before the I, giving NFETTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Confetti is small pieces of coloured tissue thrown over a bride and groom at weddings.

clue.text: More experienced nurse, one with an alternative

parts.note: SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade
the Roman numeral I is one
or is the word that offers an alternative

explanation.surface: A seasoned nurse turns out to have a stand-in available.
explanation.walkthrough: SEN (State Enrolled Nurse) was a British nursing qualification, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone senior has greater rank or longer service, and so more experience.

clue.text: Sharp feeling of hunger? You'll need cooking vessel that's good

parts.note: a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: Feeling peckish? You'll need a decent saucepan to cook with.
explanation.definitionFit: A pang is a sudden sharp pain, and hunger pangs are the classic example.

clue.text: Lumbering fellow stood out, lacking merest sign of litheness

indicators.note: out, as in out of shape, tells us the letters of fellow stood are rearranged
lacking says one letter of the fodder is left unused in the rearrangement
the merest sign is the smallest trace, just the first letter of litheness

explanation.surface: A clumsy man stands apart, without a trace of grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges FELLOW STOOD, which has eleven letters; 'lacking' says one L (the first letter of 'litheness', its 'merest sign') is left out, so the remaining ten letters make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbering means moving heavily and awkwardly, which is what a slow-footed walker does.

clue.text: In which one's asked to appear on TV?

definitions.text: In which one's asked to appear on TV?

parts.words: In which one's asked to appear on TV?
parts.note: reads as being invited onto a television show, but 'asked' means questioned: contestants are asked questions on screen

explanation.surface: Which programme invites you to be a guest on television?
explanation.walkthrough: 'asked' looks like 'invited'; read it as 'questioned', and the TV programme is one where contestants answer questions.
explanation.definitionFit: A television game where contestants answer questions is a programme built around being asked things.

clue.text: Venetian design Orlando's producing

indicators.note: the words design Orlando's produce the answer from inside themselves, across the word break

explanation.surface: A designer named Orlando is making something in Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in desIGN ORlando's. 'Venetian' stands for an Italian man, since signor is the Italian title for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from Venice is Italian, and Signor is how an Italian gentleman is addressed, like Mister.

clue.text: I'd reported being seen

indicators.note: reported means spoken out, so the clue word is the sound, not the spelling

parts.note: these words are said aloud, and what is heard is the sound this part of the answer needs

explanation.surface: Someone says they would have been noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, I'D sounds just like the answer, which means looked at.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyed means looked at or watched, so a thing eyed has been seen.

clue.text: Pressure to sharpen bid for ring

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
to hone a blade is to sharpen it
a call is a bid in bridge

explanation.surface: A jeweller under pressure tries to improve an offer for a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like jewellery, but it is the telephone sense. A call is a bid in the card game bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a ring is to telephone them, a British idiom.

clue.text: Make one university empty faculty

indicators.note: an empty faculty has had everything inside removed, leaving just its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A university merges its departments after one is left without staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To unify is to bring separate parts together into a single whole.

clue.text: Going through carefully if in pain

indicators.note: in says the word if goes inside the word for pain

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain

explanation.surface: Someone checks something closely, wondering whether it will hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sifting evidence means examining it closely, as a sieve separates fine from coarse.

clue.text: Unite around one eastern philosophy, very old?

indicators.note: around says the word for unite wraps the next pieces

parts.note: to wed is to unite in marriage
the Roman numeral I is one
Zen is a Japanese school of Buddhist thought

explanation.surface: A marriage built on Buddhist thought, between two very elderly people.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: wizened means shrivelled and wrinkled, which usually comes with great age.
explanation.definitionFit: Wizened describes skin shrunken and wrinkled with age, the look of someone elderly.

clue.text: One goes round in Rolls-Royce, too spoilt

indicators.note: in says the shuffled letters sit inside the car abbreviation
spoilt means damaged, so the letters of too are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone in a luxury car is far too pampered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoilt' rearranges TOO to OTO, and 'in' puts it inside RR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the spinning part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades.

clue.text: Son's second article on left-winger getting suppressed

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a mo is a moment, a second
the is the definite article
a Red is a communist or socialist

explanation.surface: A son's moment of attention on a left-wing activist gets stifled.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother something is to stifle it, keeping it from coming out.

clue.text: Movement to start school taking on a dozen, maybe — about right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the letter for right
maybe signals that a dozen is only one way of arranging these letters

explanation.surface: A school starts a campaign by enrolling twelve pupils, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' places SCH first. 'maybe' rearranges A DOZEN to EZANDO, and 'about' wraps that round R, giving ERZANDO.
explanation.definitionFit: Scherzando, playfully, is a musical direction often given to a lively piece or movement.

clue.text: Church inauguration? Indicate 'do 'will be organised

indicators.note: organised means put into order, so the letters of indicate and do are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions for laying on a party at church.
explanation.definitionFit: A church's dedication is the ceremony consecrating it, so it marks the building's formal opening.

clue.text: Celebrate thirteen down, apt to be excited

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of thirteen down apt are mixed

explanation.surface: A clue pointing to another entry, with its letters stirred up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thirteen down' looks like a reference to another clue, but there is no 13 Down: the words are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To go out and enjoy a wild night on the town is to celebrate lavishly.

clue.text: It takes time to get extremely rich from fishing

parts.note: rolling in it, or simply rolling, means very wealthy

explanation.surface: Getting very wealthy takes a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling', short for rolling in money, is informal for extremely rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Trolling is angling by trailing a baited line behind a moving boat.

clue.text: District's on large island in need of development

indicators.note: something needing development is still to be worked into shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A big undeveloped island in a regional plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional means belonging to an area, the way a district's affairs are local.

clue.text: In France, in love with editor, and captivated

parts.note: en is French for in
amour is French for love

explanation.surface: Someone in Paris falls for an editor and is charmed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enamoured is to be smitten and charmed by someone.

clue.text: Take top off port in garden alcove

indicators.note: removing the top of a word in a down clue drops its first letter

parts.note: a harbour is a port

explanation.surface: Instructions for a shelter by the dock in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbour is a shaded garden nook formed by trees or climbing plants.

clue.text: Reason one contralto's on record

parts.note: a log is a written record
the Roman numeral I is one
C is the abbreviation for contralto

explanation.surface: A contralto gives the reason she is on the album.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is the science of reasoning, and reason is the faculty for it.

clue.text: Foreign articles about Queen's food store

indicators.note: about means around, so the two articles surround the letter for the Queen

parts.note: la is a French article, the
der is a German article, the
R stands for Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Imported goods surround the monarch's pantry.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase gives two words: LA (French 'the') and DER (German 'the'), with R (Regina) between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a cool room or cupboard for keeping provisions.

clue.text: High ball by Lamb is a bloomer

parts.note: a lob is a ball hit or thrown high
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A lofted delivery from a cricketer called Lamb turns out to be a howler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it means a flowering plant. Charles Lamb signed his essays Elia.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a garden plant with blue flowers, so it blossoms.

clue.text: See in this a cut of pork?

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Asking whether this is a piece of pig meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Loin is a joint of meat from either side of the backbone, as in pork chops.

clue.text: State troops in operation, covered by screen

indicators.note: covered by means sitting inside, so the word for screen goes round the next pieces

parts.note: to vet is to screen or check
RM are the Royal Marines
on means working, in operation

explanation.surface: Soldiers on a mission are shown on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: RM, the Royal Marines, are British commando troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermont is one of the fifty US states, in New England.

clue.text: Huge container with sulphur in

indicators.note: in, at the end, says the sulphur symbol goes into the tank word

parts.note: a vat is a large tank
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A giant tank with sulphur inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Vast means immense or enormous in size.

clue.text: To put in container wold cause hesitation in pub

indicators.note: in says the hesitation sound goes inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
ur is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Hesitation in a bar holds up a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To inurn is to place cremated ashes in an urn.

clue.text: Padre does upset ruffian

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of padre does are mixed up

explanation.surface: A priest annoys a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, a violent criminal.
